intended_object: The K-algebra map from the polynomial ring in the strict-upper entries x_{ij} (i < j) of an n×n unitriangular matrix to the polynomial ring in the "surviving" entries (j − i ≥ r). It sends a surviving variable to itself and every other variable to 0. I inferred this from the docstring, the `killForbidden_X` lemma and the module doc.
explanation:
The body is just Mathlib's `MvPolynomial.killCompl`, applied to the subtype inclusion of the surviving index pairs. The simp lemma `killForbidden_X` confirms the intended behaviour: X_p goes to X_⟨p,hp⟩ when i + r ≤ j and to 0 otherwise. So it correctly gives the substitution map that sets the forbidden variables to zero.

It is not a standard mathematical object in its own right. It is a specific instance of a general Mathlib construction, introduced as a technical step: the module uses it to show that the stage quotient of the unitriangular coordinate ring is a polynomial algebra in the surviving entries. It is a specific map, so it is not too narrow, and it is not incorrect either.
